title.en: Accusative case: why der becomes den and ein becomes einen

summary.en: For direct objects and motion prepositions like durch, only masculine singular articles change shape.

body.en:
From season 1, episode 1.

When Werner leads Helga *durch den Bogen* and carries *den blauen Koffer* upstairs, masculine *der Koffer* changes its article to *den*. Moments later, Klara calls the station about *einen* mixed-up suitcase and wonders who leaves *einen Holzzug* with strangers.

A noun receiving the action of verbs like carry, have, find, or report stands in the accusative case, as do nouns after prepositions such as *durch* ('through') and into (*in* with motion). Here is the reassuring shortcut: feminine *die* / *eine*, neuter *das* / *ein*, and plural *die* stay completely unchanged!

Only masculine singular shifts to `-en`: *der* becomes *den*, *ein* becomes *einen*, and *kein* becomes *keinen*.

On replay, listen for that `-en` echo across *durch den Bogen*, *den blauen Koffer*, and *einen Holzzug*.
